born.why: The code prioritizes survival by using trait-based inference from past safe experiences to decide whether to taste or avoid unknown fruits, preventing unnecessary poisoning when hunger is low, while still allowing foraging when hungry enough to justify the risk.

The code prioritizes learning unknown fruits via 'taste' when safe (hunger < 90) to build knowledge, while using 'eat' only during starvation or for known-safe species when the pantry is full, ensuring long-term survival through information gain.

It balances immediate survival against long-term learning by tasting unknown fruits when hunger is low to expand safe species knowledge, while carrying known good fruits to reduce foraging effort, and eating everything only when starvation risk outweighs the cost of potential poisoning.

This code prioritizes survival by eating anything when hunger is critical, uses a pantry system to reduce foraging effort, infers safety from shared traits (smell/shape) to minimize unnecessary tasting, and avoids unknown fruits when the pantry is sufficient or hunger is low, thus balancing risk and reward for longevity.

The code prioritizes survival by treating unknown fruits with caution unless hunger is high or they share traits with previously safe foods, using trait-based inference to reduce poisoning risk while still allowing learning.

This code adds a "safety net" by tracking similar smells/shapes to infer safety for new fruits, prioritizes eating over carrying when pantry space is low or hunger is critical, and prevents seeking out high-risk unknown fruits unless starving.

The code prioritizes extreme starvation survival, avoids known poisons, carries abundant safe food for efficiency, and uses tasting to update the diary for unknown species, ensuring long-term learning and safety.

The code prioritizes safety by tasting unknown fruits unless starvation is imminent (>90 hunger), and leverages past experience to carry known good fruits when pantry space allows, optimizing long-term survival and food storage efficiency.

The code prioritizes survival by distinguishing between known poisons (avoid), known good foods (carry to pantry for efficiency), and unknown foods (taste to learn unless starving). It uses a higher hunger threshold (98) for emergency eating to prevent accidental death during the "taste" phase, and restricts exploration of new fruits until hunger is low enough that a potential poison bite won't kill her immediately.
